title: Read: place
description: One settlement, hamlet, fortress or key location by id, with the rows that join to it resolved. Answered by POST /world/place (Sim/icarus_sim/terrain_read.place_request). Every join is the writer's own field and the writing site is named in joins[].writer, because a near miss - endswith for equality, a node where the writer keyed on an id - answers a different question and looks correct.

anchor.description: What to cache. id_survives_an_age is false for hamlets and fortresses, whose ids are ordinals re-derived at every age boundary; node is the thing to key on instead.

roster_key.description: The key npcs.sites[].uid files this place under. A settlement uid unchanged for a city; hamlet-node-<node> or fortress-node-<node> for the small sites, because their ordinal ids renumber. Null for a key location, which the roster has no rows for yet.

place.description: The generator's own row, verbatim. Fields are the writing block's and are not restated here.

core.description: humans.cores[] where site_id equals settlements.sites[].id. Cities only.

seasonal_food_model.description: seasonal_food.models[] where site_id equals settlements.sites[].id. Cities only.

seasonal_food_summary.description: seasonal_food.cities[] for the same site_id. Cities only.

core_city.description: The city a hamlet or fortress answers to. core_id is a POSITION in settlements.sites, not a uid; it is checked against that site's own id before being used, because settlements.sites[].id equals its index is an invariant and not a coincidence.

post_count.description: The true number of roster rows filed under this place, whether or not they were all returned.

site_plan.description: A city, hamlet or castle plan: its identity, status and size, never its body. A city plan is most of a megabyte on a size-17 world and this read is meant to be kilobytes, so bytes states what fetching it would cost. Null on a key location, which has a location_plan instead. Kept apart from location_plan because their status fields are different vocabularies that share the word complete.

id_field.description: The field inside that block this id was matched against: city_uid, hamlet_id or fortress_id.

status.description: The planner's own word for whether this plan was fully placed, carried verbatim. The same three tokens world-output.schema.json declares for city, hamlet and castle plan items, where status is required. NOT the same question as a key location plan's status, which asks whether a plan has contents; complete is in both vocabularies and means two different things - see board/backlog/SDET-STATUS-VOCABULARY.md.

location_plan.description: A key location's plan: the same identity, status and size fields, in its own definition because its status is its own vocabulary. Null on a city, hamlet or fortress, which have a site_plan instead.

status.description: Whether this plan has contents, carried verbatim. The two tokens key-location-plans.schema.json declares for plans[], where status is required. NOT the site planners' question of whether a plan was fully placed.

post.description: A roster row projected, not copied: the full record is what the person read is for.

status.description: npc_roster's own vocabulary, carried verbatim. The same two tokens npc-roster.schema.json declares for npcs.people[], where status is required. It is one of five status vocabularies in this tree and it is NOT the hero one: use the person read for liveness resolved through the single predicate.
